description: This repo had customManagers and packageRules but never extended the org preset, so it ran on admin defaults: no graduated soak, no per-type semantic commits, no dashboard-approval gate. The repo every other repo's CI depends on was the least governed one. Its own rules below are unchanged and still win — repo config is applied after presets.

customManagers.description: The release toolchain images are named in workflow input DEFAULTS. Renovate's workflow manager pins `uses:` refs but is blind to an image tag handed to a job via an input default, so nothing would watch the toolchain a release actually runs in. Same annotated-default pattern infrastructure uses for tool versions passed to composite actions. The tag is captured, and the digest too when the default pins one (the semantic-release image is pinned as tag@sha256 since config 2.x), so a bump rewrites both; the repository comes from depName.

packageRules.description: Renovate never adds a digest to an annotated default that has none. The semantic-release toolchain default carries its digest explicitly, and Renovate keeps an existing digest current on every bump.

The release toolchain image is first-party (built and released by webgrip/semantic-release-config, tagged with the config version it carries, ADR 0005) and every estate release runs in it, so a new patch or minor toolchain must reach this repo's defaults without a dashboard tick: on 2026-10-24 semantic-release 0.3.7 and semantic-release-monorepo 0.3.6, the first images with @webgrip/semantic-release-config 1.4.0 (homelab ADR-0069's forge adapter), waited behind the org preset's dependencyDashboardApproval. A major is a new config major that changes what every caller's release does, so it stays behind the preset's dashboard approval and is never merged unattended. The semantic-release-monorepo image is retired: config 2.x builds monorepo trains itself. The semantic-release-rust image is retired: nothing used it (VIK-2321).
